name: SULLIVAN, Justice
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion reversing the trial court's dismissal and remanding the case, finding that Hyatt III does not apply to JEA and that neither the Full Faith and Credit Clause nor comity mandate dismissal.

name: COLEMAN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the initiative process was unworkable with fewer than five congressional districts, rendering the medical marijuana initiative invalid.

name: MAXWELL, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Secretary of State acted constitutionally based on existing Mississippi law recognizing five congressional districts, and the majority's decision effectively kills the citizen-initiative process.

name: CHAMBERLIN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the constitutional initiative process remains workable by interpreting 'congressional district' as the five districts existing in 1992, and the majority's ruling disables the people's right to amend the constitution.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.

name: RANDOLPH, C.J.

name: CHAMBERLIN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that PPS lacked standing because they failed to demonstrate an adverse impact different from the general public, especially since the funds were federal ARPA funds not earmarked for education.

name: BEAM, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court is not ruling on state funds but ARPA funds, which were not earmarked for educational purposes, so PPS cannot claim harm.

name: KING, P.J.
description: Dissented, argued that PPS has standing due to adverse effect from competitive advantage given to private schools and taxpayer standing, and that the bills are unconstitutional for appropriating funds to non-free schools.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.
description: Dissented, argued that PPS has standing and that Senate Bills 2780 and 3064 are unconstitutional for appropriating funds to independent schools that are not free.

name: GRIFFIS, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that JFT failed to establish standing, either in its own right or through associate standing, because it did not provide direct evidence of current JPS employees as members at the time of litigation.

name: COLEMAN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that JFT had standing because ample evidence showed it was a legitimate organization adversely impacted by JPS policies, and direct evidence of membership is not always required, especially when it is common knowledge.

name: KITCHENS, P.JJ.
description: Dissented, argued that JFT had standing, the issue was not moot, and multiple free speech violations occurred, thus the trial court's judgment should be affirmed.

name: KING, P.JJ.

name: MAXWELL, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that House Bill 1020, Section 1, violated the constitutional requirement for elected judges, while Section 4 and Section 9-1-105(2) are constitutional as they establish an inferior court with appellate oversight and allow for temporary judicial appointments for emergencies.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, arguing that the CCID court is unconstitutional due to the Legislature's failure to provide a statutory mechanism for supervision by a constitutional court.

name: KING, P.J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, joining Presiding Justice Kitchens' opinion regarding the unconstitutionality of the CCID court.

name: David M. Ishee
description: Concurred, argued that Brown's petition was successive, barred by res judicata, frivolous, and warranted sanctions including restricting future in forma pauperis filings.

name: KING, PRESIDING JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that the Court prioritizes efficiency over justice, that imposing monetary sanctions and restricting access for indigent defendants violates constitutional rights to access the court system, and that the petition should simply be found to lack merit without restricting future filings.

name: Dawn H. Beam
description: Concurred, argued that Brunson's petition was time-barred, successive, without merit, and frivolous, justifying denial and restriction of future in forma pauperis filings.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.
description: Dissented, argued that while the petition lacked merit, restricting an indigent defendant's access to courts violates constitutional rights and prioritizes efficiency over justice.

name: KING, P.J.

name: KING, P.J.

name: KING, P.J.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.

name: KING, PRESIDING JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that Buford was not illegally detained and his general consent to search his person reasonably extended to the smokeless tobacco can found in his pocket.

name: COLEMAN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the reduction to four congressional districts made the signature distribution requirement of Section 273(3) unworkable, invalidating Initiative 65.

name: MAXWELL, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation judicially kills the citizen-initiative process by wrongly applying a federal injunction to state constitutional law, which still recognizes five congressional districts.

name: CHAMBERLIN, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's ruling destroys the presumption that the Constitution can order human affairs and that Section 273(3) should be interpreted based on the five congressional districts existing in 1992 to preserve the initiative process.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.
